en.value: Wikidata item ID
The Wikidata item this item is the same as (the identity crosswalk; exact match keeps the SKOS IRI).
formatter URL
Template for a URL from the value of an external identifier.
formatter URI for RDF resource
Template for an RDF IRI from the value of an external identifier.
unit level
The level of a code, unit or section in the code's hierarchy.
act identifier
Open US Law's act_id of a section, or the prefix shared by a unit's sections.
government ID
The Census Bureau government ID (GID).
sort key
Zero-padded key that orders units, sections and steps in the code's or the process's order.
section number
The bare section number; citation keeps the full citation.
effective until
The date the provision ceases to be in force (effective date is the date from).
replaced by
The section that replaces this version.
heading text
The heading of a section, unit, decision point or rung, as searchable text.
reference type
Qualifier on references: why the provision cites the other.
quoted text
Reference: up to 400 characters of the statute, verbatim, that ground the claim.
source section
Reference: the section the quoted text is from.
pinpoint
Reference or qualifier: the subsection (B.4, (g)).
source URL
Reference: the official page a claim was made from.
retrieved
Reference: the date lexflow fetched or checked the source.
archive URL
Reference: the Internet Archive capture read when the live page refused automated reading.
determination method
Reference: how the claim or match was made.
played by
The body, office type, position type or private party that plays a role.
head position
The position that heads the agency.
position in
The agency a position belongs to (never part of).
appointed by
Who appoints the position.
supervised by
The agency or position that supervises the agency (statute only).
designee of
The position or position type a designee stands for.
authority conferred by
The section that confers the body's or role's authority; qualifiers power and quoted text.
power
Qualifier on authority conferred by: the statutory power conferred.
official website
The body's or government's official website.
contact page URL
The records page, the permits page: the page to start from.
email address
An office mailbox (mailto:), never a person's.
phone number
A main office line, never a direct line.
postal address
An office address, with any staff name removed.
described at URL
The body's Govdirectory page (linked, never copied).
step kind
The kind of a step.
recipient
The role that receives the filing or notice.
time limit
A time limit; qualifiers time unit, counted from, on expiry; reference quoted text.
time unit
Qualifier on time limit: the unit, in the law's own word.
counted from
Qualifier on time limit: the event the limit runs from.
on expiry
Qualifier on time limit: the outcome when the limit passes.
outcome
An end state of the process or step.
escalates to
Statutory escalation from a step, role or process; qualifiers quoted text, source section, pinpoint, time limit, defers to.
defers to
Referral, forwarding or concurrence to another body or process.
escalation type
The mechanism type of a rung.
form used
The government form a step or process uses.
form number
The form's number (DC-495); official text holds its URL.
fee
A fee in US dollars; qualifiers source URL, quoted text, fee basis.
fee basis
Qualifier on fee: the rule when the amount is not one number.
topic
What the process, section or form is about.
audience
Who the process is for.
question asked
The plain-language question the process answers.
review status
How far lexflow's review has gone.
checked on
The date lexflow's software last matched the quotes.
court
The court that decided the decision.
date decided
The date the decision was filed.
CourtListener ID
The CourtListener opinion cluster id.
defined in
The section that defines the term (terms plan).
scope
The unit or section a definition applies to (terms plan).
concept
The concept a defined term stands for (terms plan).
role of actor
The defined term or concept a role stands for (terms plan).
close match
skos:closeMatch to an external IRI (terms plan).
broad match
skos:broadMatch to an external IRI (terms plan).
narrow match
skos:narrowMatch to an external IRI (terms plan).
related match
skos:relatedMatch to an external IRI (terms plan).
match probability
Qualifier on exact match and the SKOS matches: the probability of the match (terms plan).
audience
Vocabulary: who a process is for.
concept
A legal concept a defined term or role stands for (the terms plan).
court
A court or court system.
currency
Vocabulary: the unit of a fee.
defined term
A term a provision defines (the terms plan).
determination method
Vocabulary: how a claim or match was made (lexflow's software, an AI verifier, a person, an HTTP check).
escalation mechanism
One rung of an escalation ladder: an appeal, petition, review, referral or complaint path the law creates.
escalation type
Vocabulary: the ten mechanism types of fixtures/authority/ladders.json.
government
A Census government: a city, county, town or similar local government.
government agency
A department, board, commission or office with standing of its own.
government form
An official form or online application a step uses.
legal code
A jurisdiction's code of laws (Virginia Code, D.C. Code, Fla. Stat.); one item per code.
legal document
A document the law names (the terms plan).
legal status
A status in law (the terms plan).
office type
A body each county, profession or record holder has (the clerk of the circuit court).
organizational unit
A division or section inside an agency.
position
A post that exists apart from its holder (Secretary of State of Florida).
position type
A post every body of a kind has (the FOIA officer of a public body).
process outcome
An end state of a process (records released, deemed denied).
reference type
Vocabulary: why one provision cites another (lexflow.law.xref.ROLES).
regulation
An administrative code section (a rule issued by an agency).
review status
Vocabulary: how far lexflow's review of an item has gone.
statutory power
What a body may do under a statute (deny a licence, extend time, decide an appeal).
statutory unit
A title, subtitle, part, chapter, article or subchapter of a code; its level is a claim.
step kind
Vocabulary: the kind of a process step (facts.steps[].kind).
time unit
Vocabulary: the unit of a time limit, in the law's own word.
topic
Vocabulary: what a process or provision is about.
unit level
Vocabulary: the level of a code, unit or section in the code's hierarchy.
applicant
A person applying for a licence, permit, benefit or filing.
business
A business or its owner.
property owner
An owner of real or personal property.
requester
A person asking a public body for records.
resident
A person who lives in the jurisdiction.
visitor
A person visiting the jurisdiction.
US dollar
United States dollar, the unit of every fee.
AI verifier
An AI verifier checked the claim against its sources.
curated
A person curated or reviewed the claim.
HTTP check
An HTTP request confirmed the page or address.
found on official page
The value was read from the body's own official page.
matched by lexflow's software
lexflow's software found the quote verbatim in the cited text.
advisory opinion
A non-binding opinion, guideline or eligibility predetermination.
compliance board
A standing body that decides complaints and can order the custodian to act.
deferral to another process
The process waits on, is tolled by, or falls back to another body's decision or another process.
delegation
A body hands its authority to a designee, officer, panel or hearing office.
external administrative review
Review or a binding ruling by a different administrative body.
internal appeal
Review, reconsideration, rehearing or a cure demand addressed to the same body (or its head, full board, or designee).
judicial review
Any court proceeding: petition, suit, mandamus, appeal, writ.
ombudsman/mediation
A neutral who tries to settle the dispute and cannot compel.
oversight/inspector general
Complaint, reporting, discipline or enforcement by an oversight office or prosecutor.
referral
The process hands the matter, a notice or a record to another body.
authority
The cited provision confers the authority the citing one exercises.
condition
The cited provision states a condition of the citing one.
definition
The cited provision defines a term the citing one uses.
exception
The cited provision is an exception to the citing one.
other
A cross-reference of no classified role.
override
The cited provision prevails over the citing one ("notwithstanding").
penalty
The cited provision sets the penalty for the citing one.
prerequisite process
The cited provision's process must be completed first.
procedure
The cited provision supplies the procedure the citing one follows.
scope
The cited provision bounds the citing one's scope.
agreed
Two independent extractions agree, or lexflow's software matched every quote and the AI verifier passed it; no person has signed.
draft
One extraction, unreviewed; may be retired, never deleted.
reviewed
A person reviewed the model and every quote was checked.
superseded
Replaced by a later item; kept, relabelled, no longer maintained.
act
An act other than a filing, notice, decision or payment.
decision
A body decides.
delivery
Records or a document are delivered.
filing
A request, application or document is filed.
hearing
A hearing is held.
inspection
Records or premises are inspected.
notice
A notice is given.
payment
A fee or tax is paid.
record
A record is made, kept or delivered.
review
A decision is reviewed.
business days
Days other than Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, in the law's words "business days".
calendar days
Days counted on the calendar.
hours
Hours.
months
Months.
weeks
Weeks.
work days
The law's own word "work days".
working days
The law's own word "working days".
years
Years.
animals
Animal licences and control.
benefits
Public benefits and assistance.
building and zoning
Building permits, zoning and land use.
business
Forming, registering and licensing a business.
courts
Court filings, tickets, small claims and probate.
criminal records
Sealing, expungement and correction of criminal records.
licensing
Occupational and activity licences and permits.
property
Deeds, assessments and property records.
public records
Requesting, inspecting and copying public records.
taxes
Assessment, billing, relief and appeal of taxes.
voting
Registering to vote and voting.
act
An act (an Illinois compiled statutes act).
article
An article.
chapter
A chapter.
code
A code of laws, or a named code inside a state's collection of codes.
division
A division.
part
A part.
section
A section.
subchapter
A subchapter.
subsection
A subsection.
subtitle
A subtitle.
title
A title.

A term a provision defines (the terms plan).
determination method
Vocabulary: how a claim or match was made (lexflow's software, an AI verifier, a person, an HTTP check).
escalation mechanism
One rung of an escalation ladder: an appeal, petition, review, referral or complaint path the law creates.
escalation type
Vocabulary: the ten mechanism types of fixtures/authority/ladders.json.
government
A Census government: a city, county, town or similar local government.
government agency
A department, board, commission or office with standing of its own.
government form
An official form or online application a step uses.
legal code
A jurisdiction's code of laws (Virginia Code, D.C. Code, Fla. Stat.); one item per code.
legal document
A document the law names (the terms plan).
legal status
A status in law (the terms plan).
office type
A body each county, profession or record holder has (the clerk of the circuit court).
organizational unit
A division or section inside an agency.
position
A post that exists apart from its holder (Secretary of State of Florida).
position type
A post every body of a kind has (the FOIA officer of a public body).
process outcome
An end state of a process (records released, deemed denied).
reference type
Vocabulary: why one provision cites another (lexflow.law.xref.ROLES).
regulation
An administrative code section (a rule issued by an agency).
review status
Vocabulary: how far lexflow's review of an item has gone.
statutory power
What a body may do under a statute (deny a licence, extend time, decide an appeal).
statutory unit
A title, subtitle, part, chapter, article or subchapter of a code; its level is a claim.
step kind
Vocabulary: the kind of a process step (facts.steps[].kind).
time unit
Vocabulary: the unit of a time limit, in the law's own word.
topic
Vocabulary: what a process or provision is about.
unit level
Vocabulary: the level of a code, unit or section in the code's hierarchy.
applicant
A person applying for a licence, permit, benefit or filing.
business
A business or its owner.
property owner
An owner of real or personal property.
requester
A person asking a public body for records.
resident
A person who lives in the jurisdiction.
visitor
A person visiting the jurisdiction.
US dollar
United States dollar, the unit of every fee.
AI verifier
An AI verifier checked the claim against its sources.
curated
A person curated or reviewed the claim.
HTTP check
An HTTP request confirmed the page or address.
found on official page
The value was read from the body's own official page.
matched by lexflow's software
lexflow's software found the quote verbatim in the cited text.
advisory opinion
A non-binding opinion, guideline or eligibility predetermination.
compliance board
A standing body that decides complaints and can order the custodian to act.
deferral to another process
The process waits on, is tolled by, or falls back to another body's decision or another process.
delegation
A body hands its authority to a designee, officer, panel or hearing office.
external administrative review
Review or a binding ruling by a different administrative body.
internal appeal
Review, reconsideration, rehearing or a cure demand addressed to the same body (or its head, full board, or designee).
judicial review
Any court proceeding: petition, suit, mandamus, appeal, writ.
ombudsman/mediation
A neutral who tries to settle the dispute and cannot compel.
oversight/inspector general
Complaint, reporting, discipline or enforcement by an oversight office or prosecutor.
referral
The process hands the matter, a notice or a record to another body.
authority
The cited provision confers the authority the citing one exercises.
condition
The cited provision states a condition of the citing one.
definition
The cited provision defines a term the citing one uses.
exception
The cited provision is an exception to the citing one.
other
A cross-reference of no classified role.
override
The cited provision prevails over the citing one ("notwithstanding").
penalty
The cited provision sets the penalty for the citing one.
prerequisite process
The cited provision's process must be completed first.
procedure
The cited provision supplies the procedure the citing one follows.
scope
The cited provision bounds the citing one's scope.
agreed
Two independent extractions agree, or lexflow's software matched every quote and the AI verifier passed it; no person has signed.
draft
One extraction, unreviewed; may be retired, never deleted.
reviewed
A person reviewed the model and every quote was checked.
superseded
Replaced by a later item; kept, relabelled, no longer maintained.
act
An act other than a filing, notice, decision or payment.
decision
A body decides.
delivery
Records or a document are delivered.
filing
A request, application or document is filed.
hearing
A hearing is held.
inspection
Records or premises are inspected.
notice
A notice is given.
payment
A fee or tax is paid.
record
A record is made, kept or delivered.
review
A decision is reviewed.
business days
Days other than Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, in the law's words "business days".
calendar days
Days counted on the calendar.
hours
Hours.
months
Months.
weeks
Weeks.
work days
The law's own word "work days".
working days
The law's own word "working days".
years
Years.
animals
Animal licences and control.
benefits
Public benefits and assistance.
building and zoning
Building permits, zoning and land use.
business
Forming, registering and licensing a business.
courts
Court filings, tickets, small claims and probate.
criminal records
Sealing, expungement and correction of criminal records.
licensing
Occupational and activity licences and permits.
property
Deeds, assessments and property records.
public records
Requesting, inspecting and copying public records.
taxes
Assessment, billing, relief and appeal of taxes.
voting
Registering to vote and voting.
act
An act (an Illinois compiled statutes act).
article
An article.
chapter
A chapter.
code
A code of laws, or a named code inside a state's collection of codes.
division
A division.
part
A part.
section
A section.
subchapter
A subchapter.
subsection
A subsection.
subtitle
A subtitle.
title
A title.

datavalue.value: The following officers shall not, except as herein otherwise provided, be affected by the adoption of the county executive form:

Any willfully false material statement or entry made by any person in any statement, form, or report required by this title shall constitute the crime of election fraud and be punishable as a Class 5 felony.

The State Board, through the Department of Elections, shall supervise and coordinate the work of the county and city electoral boards and of the registrars to obtain uniformity in their practices and proceedings and legality and purity in all elections.

The State Board may institute proceedings pursuant to § 24.2-234.1 for the removal of any member of an electoral board or general registrar by a recorded majority vote of the Board after a public hearing on related matters.
There shall be in each county and city an electoral board composed of three members who shall be qualified voters of such county or city.
Each electoral board shall meet in the month of May or June in 2007, and every four years thereafter, and shall appoint a general registrar
The registration records shall be closed during the 10 days before a primary or general election.

any person who is qualified to register to vote shall be entitled to register in person up to and including the day of the election at the office of the general registrar in the locality in which such person resides or at the polling place for the precinct in which such person resides.
the polls shall be open at each polling place at 6:00 a.m. on the day of the election and closed at 7:00 p.m. on the same day

The general registrar shall make printed ballots available for absentee voting not later than 45 days prior to any election or within three business days of the receipt of a properly completed absentee ballot application, whichever is later.
The officer shall ask the voter to present any one of the following forms of identification:

An officer of election, by a written notice given to the voter, shall inform him that a determination of his right to vote shall be made by the electoral board and advise the voter of the beginning time and place for the board's meeting and of the voter's right to be present at that meeting.

The electoral board shall meet on the day following the election and determine whether each person having submitted a provisional vote pursuant to § 24.2-653 was entitled to do so as a qualified voter in the precinct in which he offered the provisional vote.
Any registered voter may vote by absentee ballot in accordance with the provisions of this chapter in any election in which he is qualified to vote.

An application for an absentee ballot may be accepted the later of (i) 12 months before an election or (ii) the day following any election held in the twelfth month prior to the election in which the applicant is applying to vote.
The application shall be made to the appropriate registrar no later than 5:00 p.m. on the eleventh day prior to the election in which the applicant offers to vote.
The applicant's printed name and the last four digits of the applicant's social security number.

An application that is completed in person at the same time that the applicant registers to vote shall be held and processed no sooner than the fifth day after the date that the applicant registered to vote
An application shall not be required for any registered voter appearing in person to cast an absentee ballot pursuant to § 24.2-701.1 .

Any other application may be made by mail, by electronic or telephonic transmission to a facsimile device if one is available to the office of the general registrar or to the office of the Department if a device is not available locally, or by other means.
Absentee voting in person shall be available on the forty-fifth day prior to any election and shall continue until 5:00 p.m. on the Saturday immediately preceding the election.

If he does not show one of the forms of identification specified in subsection B of § 24.2-643 , he shall be allowed to vote after signing a statement, subject to felony penalties for false statements pursuant to § 24.2-1016 , that he is the named registered voter he claims to be.
A voter who does not show one of the forms of identification specified in this subsection or does not sign this statement shall be offered a provisional ballot under the provisions of § 24.2-653 .
Any registered voter offering to vote absentee in person shall provide his name and his residence address in the county or city in which he is offering to vote.

For purposes of this chapter, such offices shall be open to the public (i) a minimum of eight hours between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on the first and second Saturday and (ii) a minimum of five hours between the hours of 11:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on the second and third Sunday immediately preceding all elections.
Any applicant who is in line to cast his ballot when the office of the general registrar or voter satellite office closes shall be permitted to cast his absentee ballot that day.
The governing body of any county or city may establish, by ordinance, voter satellite offices to be used in the locality for absentee voting in person.

Not later than 55 days prior to any election, the general registrar shall post notice of all voter satellite office locations in the locality and the dates and hours of operation of each location in the office of the general registrar and on the official website for the county or city.
Any registered voter shall be eligible to file a special application to receive absentee ballots for all elections in which he is eligible to vote.
A voter shall be removed from the permanent absentee voter list if (i) the voter requests in writing to be removed from the list
the voter may request a replacement absentee ballot by the close of business for the local elections office on the Saturday before election day

A person with a disability or illness who has applied for and has been sent an absentee ballot who did not receive or has lost the absentee ballot on or before the Saturday before the election may obtain a replacement absentee ballot.

The application for an absentee ballot shall provide space for the applicant to indicate that he will require assistance to vote his absentee ballot by reason of blindness, disability, or inability to read or write.

On receipt of an application from an applicant who indicated that he will require assistance due to a visual impairment or print disability, the general registrar shall offer to provide to the applicant a ballot marking tool with screen reader assistive technology made available pursuant to § 24.2-103.2 .
